features.name: Configurable embedding provider + offline/no-network fallback
features.behavior: get_embedder() (src/braintodo/api/nodes.py) reads settings.embedding_provider ('sentence_transformer' default | 'fake'). SentenceTransformerProvider wraps model-load OSError in a clear, actionable RuntimeError instead of a raw huggingface.co connection stack trace. Fixes a real gap: production always hardcoded the real SentenceTransformerProvider with no fallback, but every existing test overrode get_embedder with FakeEmbeddingProvider, so this path had never been exercised by any test in any session - a network-restricted deploy would 500 on every POST /nodes despite a fully green suite.
features.evidence: Discovered 2026-08-24: after installing torch/torch-geometric/sentence-transformers for the first time in any session and running the FULL suite (not the fast/excluded suite), confirmed get_sentence_transformer_provider() raises a raw OSError connecting to huggingface.co in this network-restricted sandbox - i.e. F001 (Node CRUD) would 500 on every create in an offline deploy despite being marked passing. Fixed via EMBEDDING_PROVIDER setting + FakeEmbeddingProvider fallback + clear RuntimeError. Verified both directions: (1) default 'sentence_transformer' with no network reachable raises RuntimeError with actionable message (was raw OSError before fix); (2) EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=fake exercised through the REAL api.nodes.get_embedder -> NodeRepository dependency-injection path (not a test override) successfully returns 201 on POST /nodes with a real embedding vector. Full suite re-run after fix: 118 passed, 1 skipped (test_neo4j_store.py self-skips, no live Neo4j in this sandbox), ruff check . clean. UPDATE 2026-08-25: a second session (running on a machine with real internet access, unlike this sandbox) caught a real gap in the original test_sentence_transformer_unreachable_raises_actionable_error test - it asserted real network failure rather than mocking it, so it only passed in a network-restricted environment and would have tried to genuinely download the model (slow/flaky, and not actually testing the error-wrapping logic) on any machine with working internet. Fixed by monkeypatching sentence_transformers.SentenceTransformer to raise OSError, making the test hermetic regardless of the running environment's actual network state. The same session also resolved the previously-flagged pre-existing mypy error (SentenceTransformerProvider.dimension: int | None vs int) via an explicit dimension: int class annotation + int(dim) if dim is not None else 384 fallback. Both fixes independently re-verified in a torch-installed sandbox (not just trusted from the reporting session, which had only run the fast/--ignore suite and not the full one): pytest -q -> 118 passed, 1 skipped (unchanged); ruff check . -> clean; mypy src tests -> 0 errors in 85 files (previously 1 pre-existing error, now genuinely resolved, not just claimed).

features.name: Clustering service upgrade: Leiden algorithm + configurable resolution + semantic cluster labels
features.behavior: Replace/augment the Louvain-based ClusterService (F006) with the Leiden algorithm (guarantees well-connected communities, higher modularity quality, faster convergence than Louvain - Louvain can produce internally-disconnected communities, Leiden fixes this). GET /clusters accepts an optional resolution query param (default matches current behavior) to let callers trade off cluster granularity. Each returned cluster also gets an auto-generated label derived from its member nodes' text embeddings (e.g. the node closest to the cluster's embedding centroid, or its title) so clusters are human-readable ('Auth & Security', 'GNN Pipeline') instead of just numeric ids.
features.evidence: 2026-08-28. Replaced Louvain with python-igraph + leidenalg (RBConfigurationVertexPartition with deterministic seed=42). Cluster model extended with optional label: str | None. Added semantic cluster labeling via centroid cosine similarity over member embeddings (falling back to None when no members have embeddings). GET /clusters accepts resolution query param (gt=0, default 1.0). tests/test_clustering.py (13 tests) covers two dense groups, isolated nodes, empty graphs, determinism across calls, resolution sensitivity, centroid/cosine math, semantic labels, and missing-embedding fallbacks. tests/test_clusters_api.py (4 tests) covers connected clusters, empty graphs, resolution parameter, and positive validation (422 on <=0). Full suite: pytest -q -> 123 passed, 1 skipped; ruff check . clean; mypy src tests clean.

features.name: Optional: persisted 3D node layout position (x, y, z)
features.behavior: Node model gains optional x, y, z float fields so a 3D layout position can be persisted and stay stable across reloads/sessions, instead of being recomputed from scratch by the client's force simulation every time. Deliberately optional/low-priority: the 3D graph view (FE025) works today with a purely client-computed, ephemeral layout (matching how the existing 2D d3-force layout already works) - this feature only matters if users want their 3D arrangement to persist rather than re-settle on every load.
features.evidence: Planned 2026-08-25. Deliberately deferred/optional: confirmed the 3D graph requirement (FE025) does NOT require any backend change to function - 3D layout, like the existing 2D layout, can be computed entirely client-side from the same /nodes and /edges data already served. This entry exists only to track the persistence enhancement if it's later wanted, not as a blocker for FE025.
